questions.q: What does Orenstein say about most female characters girls see on screen?
a: They often exist mainly as objects of male desire
They are written as complex role models
They rarely appear in popular movies
They usually hold powerful jobs
questions.why: Lesson 1 says many female characters have little personality and serve male lust.

questions.q: What happens when parents avoid talking about sex, according to the summary?
a: Girls face confusion, stress and mixed messages
Girls simply learn from friends instead
Girls become more independent and confident
Girls delay dating until they are older
questions.why: Lesson 2 says silence leaves girls torn between exploring sexuality and staying virtuous.

questions.q: What mixed message does the summary say girls receive about sexuality?
a: They are pushed to explore desire yet told to stay virtuous
They are told sex is natural but also dangerous
They are encouraged to date but not to fall in love
They are praised for modesty but rewarded for attention
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes girls being labeled prudes or sluts whichever way they behave.

questions.q: What does the Dutch example show about comprehensive sex education?
a: Teens start later and report more pleasant first experiences
Teens start earlier but use protection more
Teens avoid sex until they leave school
Teens learn mostly from their parents at home
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Dutch teens become active later and describe losing their virginity as pleasant.

questions.q: What does research say about abstinence-only education?
a: It leaves students unprepared and raises pregnancy risk
It delays sexual activity better than other methods
It works when parents also give consent
It has no measurable effect either way
questions.why: Lesson 3 says students given abstinence-only education are 60 percent more likely to have an unwanted pregnancy.
